slides.title: Supportable at *3am*.
slides.body:
Five things.
None of them are products.

slides.title: 1. Consistent naming
slides.body:
At 3am you type the name before you think.
Naming is *the index* into everything else.

slides.title: 2. One source of truth
slides.body:
Two systems disagree about a VLAN. Which wins?
If it's “ask Dave,” *Dave is asleep*.

slides.title: 3. Out-of-band that works
slides.body: Can you reach a console while the uplink is down, without transiting *what's broken*?

slides.title: 4. Backups someone restored
slides.body:
A green checkmark is an unverified claim.
The backup is rarely the problem. *The restore is.*

slides.title: 5. One named owner
slides.body:
Not a team alias.
“Escalate to Network” is a *queue*, not an owner.

slides.title: None of it is a product
slides.body: Not one of these five appears in a *design review*.

slides.title: At 3am nobody is clever
slides.body: You only have what you wrote down while it was *daylight*.

slides.title: Which one would you fail tonight?
slides.body:
Naming. Source of truth. Out-of-band.
Restores. An owner.

Follow *@mzsnetworks*
